subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw core support native cross-gateway session routing now, and if so should this be a narrow `gateway.peers` session-tool API or part of a broader federation/bridge contract?
rationale: The PR crosses gateway trust, message delivery, and session-state boundaries while adding new config and model-facing tool parameters, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent API or security model.

options.title: Design Federation Contract First
options.body: Use the linked issue and federation discussion to define peer identity, authorization, replay, delivery, and transcript ownership before merging code.

options.title: Sponsor Narrow Peers
options.body: Allow a refreshed PR only if it keeps URL validation centralized, fixes the protocol bugs, documents upgrade behavior, and provides live two-gateway proof.

options.title: Defer Core Routing
options.body: Keep multiple gateways isolated for now and point users to documented operator-owned bridges or plugins until maintainers want a core trust boundary.

recommendation.title: Design Federation Contract First
recommendation.body: Use the linked issue and federation discussion to define peer identity, authorization, replay, delivery, and transcript ownership before merging code.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for session-tool routing and security scoping is in this person's prior session-tool work.
